text:
jamie: Heads up — automated cutover for eu-gpu-pool failed during the gradual traffic shift. Canary controller aborted with 503s.

maria: ugh, saw alerts. any obvious errors in the rollout logs?

jamie: pasteshort logs: `Error scheduling pod: 0/6 nodes are available: 6 node(s) didn't match node selector, 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu`. The new nodepool was created but nodes had label `gpu-type: a100-v2` while helm values expected `gpu: a100`.

riley: that label mismatch looks like the helm chart's nodeSelector changed in PR #482. GitOps applied it, TF didn't update nodepool labels (we pin labels in infra). Drift.

maria: so the sequence was: GitOps deploy updated Deployment.nodeSelector -> scheduler couldn't place canary pods -> canary controller saw failures -> automation rolled back traffic but preStop hook had already scaled down old replicas?

jamie: exactly. Helm pre-delete/pre-stop hook ran for the old ReplicaSet as part of our blue/green lifecycle and scaled old set to 0 prematurely. There was a race: new pods never scheduled, old were scaled down, brief outage.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0312 (brief 90s outage for /v1/generate in eu region)

riley: reproduce steps I used: `kubectl describe pod <canary-pod>` -> nodeAffinity mismatch + `kubectl get nodes -L gpu-type` showed new nodes labeled differently. Also `terraform state show module.nodepool.aws_eks_node_group.this` shows label map has `gpu = a100` still.

maria: workaround for now: revert GitOps change to previous nodeSelector, revert traffic shift, and force GitOps to wait until node labels match. Can someone run the revert?

jamie: I'm doing the rollback now: `flux reconcile kustomization infra --with-source` then `kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-inference --to-revision=3 -n inference`. I'll follow with canary abort in CD pipeline.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued by jamie. Will post status.

jamie: rollback done. traffic back to baseline. ops-bot updated INC-2026-0312: mitigated.

riley: root cause: config split between infra (Terraform-managed nodepool labels) and app (helm chart nodeSelector). A GitOps push changed app expectations without infra change. Canary automation had no preflight check for node selector satisfaction.

maria: action items: 1) Add pre-deploy gate in progressive delivery controller to validate nodeSelector/affinity resolves to >= desired capacity of schedulable nodes. 2) Update helm hooks to avoid scaling down old ReplicaSet until new pods are Running and Ready for X seconds. 3) Add terraform plan check step in CD to detect infra drift when app chart changes nodeSelector/affinity. 4) Postmortem note.

riley: I'll open PRs: one to the canary controller to add a `nodeReadinessCheck` precondition; one to our helm chart to convert the preStop hook into a lifecycle that waits on `readinessProbe` of new pods.

jamie: also we should consider using a label normalization layer in reconcile: if app wants `gpu-type: a100-v2` but infra labels `gpu: a100`, we can map accepted aliases at admission/gate time and warn on mismatch.

maria: concerning cost — this drift came from an infra change earlier where we introduced `a100-v2` to test perf; terraform change wasn't promoted to prod labels to avoid mass reprovision. We need clearer process around experimental nodepools vs production nodeSelectors.

riley: agreed. I'll add a checklist to the infra runbook: any app nodeSelector change must be accompanied by terraform nodepool label change or use a tolerant nodeAffinity + tolerations approach.

jamie: follow-up: let's patch Canary controller today with a conservative fix: if new pods have unschedulable reason for > 30s, abort shift and keep old replicas until manual verify. Small PR incoming.

deploy-bot: PR submitted: github.com/redwood-inference/canary-controller/pull/129 — adds preflight node-scheduler check and extends canary hold timeout.

maria: nice. schedule a quick runbook update and add an automated TF plan step in our CI for chart changes that touch scheduling fields.

riley: note for on-call: if you see `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` during a progressive delivery, first check node labels and nodepool drift before flipping traffic.

jamie: thanks all. after PR merges we'll re-run a staged cutover with stricter preflight. :thumbsup:
